640:
In the case of a use not specifically mentioned in this division, the requirements for off-street parking facilities shall be determined by the zoning board. Such determination shall be based upon the requirements set forth for the most comparable use specified in this division.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 18-1(d))
641:
The zoning board may, at its discretion, reduce the minimum number of parking spaces required for a specific use, provided that sufficient evidence is presented justifying the need for reduction in the requirements and every effort has been made to provide off-street parking in accordance with the stipulations of this division.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 18-1(e))
644:
The purpose of this division is to provide regulations to ensure the adequate provision of off-street loading and unloading space.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 18-2(a))
645:
Every building or structure or lot used for business, trade, or industry shall provide space as established herein for the loading and unloading of vehicles off the public street or alley. Such space shall have access to a public street or alley. Such space shall be arranged so that no vehicle is required to back into a public street, road or highway in order to leave the premises. Specific space requirements are as follows:
Retail business services: ten percent of the floor area.
Wholesale and industrial: five percent of the floor area.
Bus and truck terminals: sufficient space to accommodate the maximum number of buses or trucks that will be stored and loading or unloading at the terminal at any one time.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 18-2(b))
648:
A customary home occupation is a gainful occupation or profession conducted by members of a family residing on the premises and conducted entirely within the dwelling.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 16-5)
649:
The following customary home occupations, subject to the requirements of the definition provided in this division, are permitted as customary home occupations:
Barbershops and beauty shops operated by not more than two members of the residence.
Artist, dressmaker, seamstress, tailor and interior decorator.
The professional office of architect, accountant, lawyer, engineer, doctor or dentist.
Teaching, including tutoring, musical instruction, or dancing, but limited to three pupils at a given time.
Any similar use which upon review by the zoning board is deemed to be a home occupation by reason or acceptance as a home occupation in the community.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 16-5)
650: Before a home occupation shall be permitted, property owners within a 1,500-foot radius shall be notified at least 15 days prior to a meeting of the city zoning board, which shall grant a home occupation permit upon showing that this section has been complied with.
651: A home occupation permit may be denied by the zoning board if, in their judgment, such occupation will be hazardous or injurious to the welfare of the community, and that this article has not been complied with.
652:
Generally. Customary home occupations shall meet the following requirements: The office must be situated in the same dwelling unit as the home of the occupant. The residential character of that dwelling unit may not be changed. There shall be not more than one assistant employed other than the immediate members of the family residing on the property. The necessary functions of the home occupation shall not occupy over 20 percent of the floor area of the dwelling unit.
Exterior appearance. Dwellings housing customary home occupations shall display no stock in trade outside the dwelling, and no alteration to any building shall indicate from the exterior that the building is being utilized in whole or in part for any purposes other than a residential unit, including permitted accessory buildings.
Signs. The dwelling may display one nameplate or sign for each dwelling unit, subject to city sign regulations, indicating the name of the occupant or any permitted occupation, excluding flashing or animated types.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 16-5)
653: Where special equipment is used, the building and technical codes of the city shall govern installation, including electrical wiring and plumbing.
656:
This division is intended to permit greater flexibility in the development of residential areas and establish a review process by the zoning board for such development plans.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 16-6.1)
657:
Each planned unit development shall be subject to independent review and approval by the zoning board. This review process shall conform in general to the subdivision regulations of the city. In addition, the requirements of this section must be met.
The developer shall submit a site plan to the zoning board for review and approval. The zoning board shall approve or disapprove the site plan within 30 days after submittal. The site plan shall include the following: Total acreage in the tract proposed for the PUD; Street access and street layout; Arrangement of existing and proposed buildings and structures; Existing and proposed land uses throughout the tract; Topography by contours at intervals of at least five feet and extending at least 200 feet outside the tract; Name, date, north arrow, and graphic scale; A vicinity map showing the relationship of the proposed PUD to surrounding development; The location and dimensions of off-street parking spaces; The location and size of all proposed utility and storm drainage facilities and solid waste collection points; Such other information as the zoning board may deem necessary because of physical characteristics peculiar to the particular development.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 16-6.6)
659:
The minimum size of any tract zoned and developed as a planned unit development shall be five acres. Such PUD shall also have permanent, paved access to a public road.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 16-6.3)
660:
A maximum of five percent of the total area of the development may be devoted to commercial, retail or professional uses.
A maximum of 75 percent of the remaining (noncommercial) area of the development may be devoted to residential use. This percentage includes streets, parking areas, private yards and courts, and accessory residential uses.
A minimum of 25 percent of the remaining (noncommercial) area of the development shall be devoted to recreational and/or open space. This percentage may include public and semi-public buildings, recreational facilities and buildings, and common open space.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 16-6.4)
661:
Any building established in connection with a PUD that cannot properly be served by emergency or service vehicles from an abutting street shall be made accessible to such vehicles by a paved driveway with a width of not less than 20 feet, exclusive of parking space.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 16-6.5(a))
662:
The off-street parking facilities established in connection with a PUD shall be of such a design that it will not interfere with the safe movement of pedestrians, the efficient flow of traffic, and will not interfere with the access of service and delivery vehicles. The requirements for off-street parking for uses in a PUD shall follow the general off-street parking requirements of this chapter.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 16-6.5(b))
663:
All buildings within a PUD shall be at least 20 feet apart, but at least 40 feet apart when front to front.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 16-6.5(c))
664:
In residential buildings, no single row of dwelling units which are physically attached shall be greater than 200 feet in length.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 16-6.5(d))
665:
Except as otherwise specifically provided in this article, there shall be no minimum lot size, no minimum setbacks, and no minimum lot widths within the PUD; provided, however, that measures are taken to provide reasonable visual and acoustical privacy for dwelling units. There shall be provided a minimum of a 20-foot buffer between any PUD and adjacent residential areas. Further, each dwelling unit shall have access to a street, walkway, or other common area, and no structure or building shall be erected within 15 feet of any other structures.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 16-6.5(e))
666:
Adequate provisions for water supply, sanitary sewerage, and storm drainage shall be installed by the developer in accordance with accepted engineering principles.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 16-6.5(f))
669:
The purpose of this division is to provide for the continuation and, within a suitable period of time, elimination of existing uses of property that that did not conform to the requirements of this chapter on December 1, 2003.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 17-1)
671:
Application; renewal. An application for a temporary use permit authorizing temporary occupancy shall be submitted to the mayor and city council for approval. Upon approval, such temporary permit shall be issued for a period not exceeding one year. Applicant can seek permit renewal in 12-month increments if necessity continues beyond the initial year.
Construction projects. A temporary use permit may be issued by the city for an appropriate period of time not to exceed 12-month increments for nonconforming buildings, structures or uses incidental to and necessary to provide for the preparation of a construction site or the completion of a construction project. The owner of such temporary nonconforming use must agree to remove the temporary use upon expiration of the permit.
Sick or infirm resident. A manufactured home may be placed on a lot occupied by a permanent building where, for humanitarian reasons, it is necessary to provide for the care of a sick or infirm immediate family member on that lot. Once the necessity for such use terminates, the manufactured home must be removed within 45 days.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 17-4)
673:
Ground-mounted solar collection system means a solar energy system that is directly installed in the ground and is not attached or affixed to an existing structure. This system can include pole-mounted systems that allow for the tracking of the sun.
Power inverter means a device that inverts the direct current (DC) electricity produced by a solar PV system into usable alternating current (AC).
Solar electric power generation. Comprises non-residential establishments primarily engaged in operating solar electric power generation facilities. These facilities use energy from the sun to produce electric energy.
Solar farm means a term used to describe large-scale solar energy systems. These facilities are typically larger tracts of land containing hundreds of arrays of photovoltaic panels covering most of a parcel.
Solar glare means the effect produced by light reflecting from a solar panel with an intensity sufficient to cause annoyance, discomfort, or loss in visual performance and visibility.
Solar panel means, for the purpose of this article, a solar panel may refer to a solar module or surface component of a flat plate collector. Solar panels are meant to absorb, not reflect, sunlight.
Solar project means a facility for solar electric power generation including, but not limited to, a solar farm. A solar project may be a ground mounted system or roof mounted system of a size larger than required to power one single family residence.
(Res. of 5-6-2025(1), § 1)
674:
Once a building permit is issued for a solar project, the applicant must commence construction within six months of issuance, or the permit shall lapse. Construction must be completed within 18 months of permit issuance unless the permit expressly provides otherwise. Exceptions to these time limitations may be made at permit issuance for good cause. For tax purposes, the solar project shall be considered complete and operational no later than 12 months after commencement of construction.
(Res. of 5-6-2025(1), § 1)
675:
Glint and glare. Solar components must have a UL listing and must be designed with an anti-reflective coating(s). All construction shall comply with the National Electric Code and applicable building codes. The developer shall graphically demonstrate through the use of renderings, photographs, or similar credible media that the proposed solar collection device or combination of devices shall be designed and located to avoid glare or reflection onto adjacent properties and adjacent roadways, and shall not interfere with traffic or create a safety hazard. Screening, using fencing of at least eight feet in height, along with vegetative buffers placed outside the security fence, shall be provided along all sides of the project that face a public road or a residential area. If it is determined by the planning commission that buffering or screening is needed, one or more of the following may be implemented: On-site mature vegetation exists at a minimum height of ten feet and a depth of 75 feet between the security fence and adjacent properties or rights-of-way; or A single row of evergreens in combination with mature vegetation, installed at a minimum height of five feet, and achieving opaqueness and a minimum height of ten feet within five years; or A double row of off-set evergreens, absent mature vegetation installed at a minimum height of five feet, and achieving opaqueness and a minimum height of ten feet within five years.Panels are to be located and situated so that glare does not create a distraction or nuisance to traffic or adjacent residential properties. An engineer or qualified consultant must submit a statement that the glint and glare will not be offensive to residents or traffic.
Lot size. The minimum lot size required for a ground-mounted solar collection system shall be three acres. This excludes any roof-mounted systems.
Set backs. A minimum building setback of 250 feet where abutting residential property and 75 feet from public rights-of-way is required for ground mounted systems. This excludes any roof-mounted systems.
Height limitations. No structure shall exceed a height greater than ten feet, except for existing poles and overhead wiring. This is measured from the finished grade at the base of the structure to its highest point. This would exclude any roof-mounted systems.
Roof mounted systems. Roof-mounted panels shall not extend beyond the perimeter of the building on which the system is mounted or constructed. The total height of the solar panels shall not exceed the maximum building height of the underlying zoning district. Elevation drawings must be submitted to show: The highest finished slope of the solar collector and the slope of the finished roof surface on which it is to be mounted. The overall layout of the panels with the distance to the roof edge and any parapets on the building.
Interconnection lines. All power lines from a ground-mounted solar energy system shall be located underground, excluding existing utilities.
Noise level limitations. Inverter noise shall not exceed 40 decibels at the property line on which the system is located.
Controlled access. Access to the site must be controlled by a fence and locked gate of at least eight feet in height, with emergency access allowed 24/7 to emergency/governmental authorities.
Parking. The minimum number of parking spaces shall be one space for every two employees on the shift of greatest employment, plus one space for every vehicle used for work-related purposes.
Airport. Solar panels shall not be placed in the vicinity of any airport in any manner that would interfere with airport flight patterns. Any proposed solar system within two miles of an airport shall present evidence of a review by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) that indicates that the proposed solar system would not interfere with the normal operation of aircraft in the area.
Historic districts. No solar project shall be located in a designated historic district.
Environmentally sensitive areas. Solar projects proposed for development in an environmentally sensitive (i.e. wetland, or any other that is designated as such by local, state, or federal regulations) area must provide an environmental impact statement for evaluation prior to approval.
Signage. The manufacturer's and/or installer's identification and appropriate warning signs shall be posted in a clear and visible manner at the site. A warning sign concerning voltage must be placed on the main gate and must include the name and contact phone number for the solar energy system operator in case of an emergency. There shall be no commercial signage attached to any project fencing.
Other conditions. Those that provide adequate protection for adjacent residential prope[rty] lines may be deemed reasonable and appropriate for the type of system and may be added by the planning commission.
(Res. of 5-6-2025(1), § 1)
677:
Electrical disconnect. The electrical disconnect switch shall be clearly identified and accessible at all times to emergency personnel. The owner must file a map with the Lincolnton Fire Department, depicting the location of the disconnect switch. The owner shall supply for filing with these agencies all emergency contact information.
Compliance. The developer/owner shall at all times construct and operate the facility in compliance with local, state, and federal guidelines as to soil erosion and sedimentation, storm water management, and all other environmental, cultural, and historical regulations. The owner shall operate the facility in compliance with any interconnection requirements from appropriate public utilities or public utility regulatory agencies.
Failure to proceed and abandonment. The developer shall submit a decommissioning plan with the initial application to the planning commission for approval. In the event the developer/owner ceases operation of the solar project or begins but does not complete construction of the project, the developer/owner shall restore the site according to the decommissioning plan. Any solar collection device or combination of devices that is not operated for a continuous period of 12 months and for which there are no applications pending for permitted use of the structure at the end of such 12-month period shall be considered abandoned, whether or not the owner or operator intends to make use of the device(s). The owner of an abandoned solar collection device(s) shall be under a duty to remove such device(s) under the decommissioning plan. To the extent allowed by state law, the cost for removal of such device(s) must be sufficiently bonded before the commencement of the project, with the city council being listed as payee in order to ensure timely removal of the devices upon decommissioning. The amount of the bond will be determined by the public service commission or by a certified contractor. A bond certificate must be presented to the city each year, verifying that the bond has been renewed. The bond must remain in effect for as long as the solar farm exists. If such device(s) is/are not removed within a reasonable time, not to exceed three months after receipt of notice from the governing authority notifying the owner of such abandonment, the governing authority may remove the device(s) and use the bond proceeds to pay for the costs of removal. Delay by the governing authority in taking action shall not in any way waive the governing authority's right to take action.
(Res. of 5-6-2025(1), § 1)
681:
The purpose of this article is to provide standards and regulations to protect the health, safety and general welfare of the residents of the city. The city recognizes that manufactured housing meets the needs of city residents for affordable housing and iscompatible with site-built housing if developed in accordance with comparable standards. These regulations shall govern the use and operation of all manufactured homes on single lots within the incorporated limits of the city. It is the intent of this article to empower the building official and the city tax commissioner to review and issue, if all requirements are met by the applicant, the appropriate permits and decals for manufactured homes within the incorporated limits of the city.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 14-1(a))
682:
The requirements of this article do not apply to recreational vehicles because they are not acceptable for permanent occupancy and may be used for a maximum of 90 consecutive days as a temporary residence. All recreational vehicles must display a current state license plate sticker before movement. Building permits will not be issued for recreational vehicles.
Permanent connection of recreational vehicles to water, sewer or electrical service is prohibited. Installation of recreational vehicles on piers and jacks permanently is also prohibited.
(Ord. of 12-2003, §§ 14-6, 14-7(c))
683:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Manufactured home means any structure, transportable in one or more sections, which:
In the traveling mode, is eight body feet or more in width or 40 body feet or more in length; or
When erected on site, is 320 or more square feet; and
Is built on a permanent chassis and is designed to be used a dwelling with or without a permanent foundation when connected to the required utilities and includes the plumbing, heating, air-conditioning, and electrical systems contained therein;except that such term shall include any structure which meets all the requirements of this definition except the size requirements and with respect to which the manufacturer voluntarily files a certification required by the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development and complies with the standards established under the National Manufactured Housing Construction and Safety Standards Act of 1974, 42 U.S.C. 5401 et seq.
New manufactured home means any manufactured home that has not been previously used as a residence, has not been titled, and complies with the current standards established under the National Manufactured Housing Construction and Safety Standards Act of 1974, 42 USC 5401 et seq. Compliance shall be evidenced by presence of a HUD certification label and manufacturer's data plate in accordance with 24 CFR 3280, Manufactured Homes Construction and Safety Standards.
Pre-owned/used manufactured home means any manufactured home that has been previously used as a residential dwelling and has been titled and complies with the standards established under the National Manufactured Housing Construction and Safety Standards Act of 1974, 42 USC 5401 et seq. Compliance shall be evidenced by inspection by the building official or his designated representative.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 14-1; Ord. of 4-2-2024, § 3)
684:
Every person, firm, corporation, or other entity holding title to or possessing a manufactured home that is placed or located within the city limits, shall report the location of the home to, and obtain a location decal for said manufactured home from the county tax commissioner annually, no later than April 1 of each year. Such location decal shall be designated in such manner and affixed to the manufactured home in such manner as to cause it to be easily visible for inspection.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 14-3)
687:
All applications for manufactured permits under this article shall be submitted to the building official. The building official shall make an investigation of all applicants and shall make a determination regarding the applicant or owner's compliance with the provisions of this article.
The building official shall render a decision regarding approval or disapproval of the manufactured home permit within 14 days of the building official's receipt of the application and any other documents required under this article.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 14-6(c))
688:
Any applicant or owner who alleges there is an error in, or who is aggrieved by a decision of the building official in the administration, enforcement, or interpretation of this article, may file a written appeal with the zoning board which states the grounds for such appeal. The zoning board is hereby authorized to hear and decide said appeal. The zoning board reserves the right to establish the process for such an appeal, including creation of forms and other documents.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 14-6(c))
689:
Notwithstanding any other provision of this Code, any owner or person who moves, assists in moving, or transports into the city or moves a manufactured home from one location in the city to another location in the city without a city manufactured home permit shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and shall be punished by a fine of not less than $200.00 nor more than $1,000.00 or by imprisonment for not more than 12 months, or both.
Any applicant or owner who shall willfully violate any other provision of this article shall be guilty of a misdemeanor punishable by a fine of not less than $100.00 per day or more than $1,000.00 per day for each day that such violation has continued or shall continue.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 14-4(f))
692:
Any owner of a manufactured home, whether locating or relocating said manufactured home within the city, shall file an application, together with a fee in the amount established by the city council, for a building permit at city hall. All city water and sewer tap fees must be paid prior to obtaining a building permit. The building official shall inspect the site and shall issue a building permit if the site is appropriate for placement of a manufactured home and the requisite water and sewer fees have been paid.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 14-4(a))
693:
Compliance required. No new manufactured home shall be moved into or within the city until the following conditions have been met: Location decal. A valid location decal must be obtained from the tax commissioner's office, a copy of which must be forwarded to the building official. Site plan. A site plan for the proposed location of the new manufactured home must be completed, a copy of which must be forwarded to the building official. Application. An application for a new manufactured home permit shall be made on forms developed for that purpose and shall be submitted to the building official for review and approval in accordance with this article.
Inspection; issuance of permit. Upon completion of the preceding conditions, the building official shall review and determine whether the proposed new manufactured home is in compliance with the requirements established by this article. The building official shall issue a new manufactured home permit or deny the request after the application has been fully reviewed.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 14-4(b))
694:
Compliance required. No pre-owned or used manufactured home shall be moved into or within the city until the conditions provided in this section have been met.
Location decal. A valid location decal must be obtained from the tax commissioner's office, a copy of which must be forwarded to the building official.
Application. An application for a pre-owned or used manufactured home permit shall be made on forms developed for that purpose and shall be submitted to the building official for review and approval in accordance with this article. The application for a pre-owned or used manufactured home permit shall be made on forms developed for that purpose and shall be submitted to the building official for review and approval in accordance with this article.
Site plan. A site plan for the proposed location of the pre-owned or used manufactured home must be completed, a copy of which must be forwarded to the building official.
Transport permit. A transport permit must be obtained from the building official. To obtain a transport permit, an applicant shall meet the following conditions: Affidavit of compliance with code standards. The applicant must provide a notarized affidavit signed by the applicant that the pre-owned or used manufactured home meets health and safety standards required by the land development code and this article. The affidavit shall be made on forms developed and provided for by the city for that purpose. Bond. The applicant must provide a $1,000.00 refundable guarantee of condition bond; such bond shall be by cash, certified check, bank check or money order. Upon completion of setup, all required repairs and issuance of a certificate of occupancy, $500.00 of the $1,000.00 guarantee of condition bond will be refunded to the applicant/owner. The guarantee of condition bond shall be forfeited in its entirety $1,000.00 should the applicant or owner: Fail to complete the necessary corrections required to bring the home into compliance with this article within 90 days of issuance of a manufactured home permit; or Fail to demolish or remove from the city within 14 days any pre-owned or used manufactured home which has been declared unsafe for human occupation by the building official.
Pre-installation inspection. Upon issue of transport permit an inspection will be completed by the building official at the location in which the manufactured home will be installed to ensure the manufactured home meets the standards established by this article. If the manufactured home does not meet these standards, the building official shall approve or disapprove the manufactured home for installation by written report. The report shall list defects or code violations found during the pre-installation inspection with corrective action required to obtain compliance with this article. Manufactured homes installed or setup on lots or parcels within the confines of the county or city may be inspected on or at the original site prior to relocation to a new lot or parcel. In no case shall any pre-owned or used manufactured home be relocated within the city prior to the completion of the pre-installation inspection.
Issuance of permit. Upon determination by the building official that the pre-owned or used manufactured home will meet the minimum manufactured home standards provided in this article, by condition or corrective action to be performed, a manufactured home permit will be issued for the home.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 14-4(c), (d))
695:
Utility services such as water, sewer, gas and electricity shall not be provided to any manufactured home until the building official determines that the requirements of this article have been met. The building official shall then issue a certificate of occupancy. No manufactured home shall be occupied or used until after the building official shall have issued a certificate of occupancy therefor. The certificate of occupancy shall be evidence that these regulations have been met, and utility service may then be provided.
(Ord. of 12-2003, §§ 14-2, 14-5)
698:
All manufactured homes shall comply with the following minimum standards:
Compliance with HUD code. Every pre-owned or used manufactured home located or relocated in the city shall be in accordance with the Federal Manufactured Housing Construction and Safety Standards Act, 42 USC 5401—5445 (the HUD code) and shall not have been altered in such a way that the home no longer meets HUD code.
Interior condition. Every floor, interior wall, and ceiling of a pre-owned manufactured home shall be in sound condition. Doors and windows shall be operable, watertight and in good working condition. The floor system shall be in sound condition and free of warping, holes, water damage, or deterioration.
Exterior condition. The exterior of all pre-owned manufactured homes shall be free of loose or rotting boards or timbers and any other conditions that might admit rain or moisture to the interior portions of the walls or to occupied spaces. The exterior siding shall be free of rot and rust. Roofs shall be structurally sound and have no obvious defects that might admit rain or cause moisture to collect on the interior portion of the home. The bottom board or under board shall be continuous and free of defects. All plumbing, heating, ventilating, air conditioning, and electrical connections shall be sealed to the bottom board/under board to prevent rodent and insect infestation.
Sanitary facilities. Every plumbing fixture, water, and waste pipe of a pre-owned manufactured home shall be in a sanitary working condition when properly connected, and shall be free from leaks and obstructions. Each home shall contain a kitchen sink. Each bathroom shall contain a lavatory and water closet. At least one bathroom shall contain a tub or shower facilities. Each of these fixtures shall be checked upon being connected to ensure they are in good working condition.
Heating system. Heating systems shall be safe and in working condition. Unvented fuel-fired space heaters shall be prohibited.
Electrical system. Electrical systems (switches, receptacles, fixtures, etc.) shall be properly installed and wired and shall be in working condition. Distribution panels shall be in compliance with the approved listing, complete with required breakers, with all unused openings covered with solid covers approved and listed for that purpose. The home shall be subject to an electrical continuity test to ensure that all metallic parts are properly bonded. Aluminum wiring smaller than #6 American wire gauge shall be prohibited.
Hot water supply. Each home shall contain a water heater in safe and working condition.
Egress windows. Each bedroom of a manufactured home shall have at least one operable window of sufficient size to allow egress if necessary.
Ventilation. The kitchen in the home shall have at least one working domestic hood system or other ventilation device.
Smoke detectors. Each pre-owned manufactured home shall contain one operable battery-powered smoke detector in each bedroom and in the kitchen, which must be installed in accordance with the manufacturer's recommendations.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 14-4(e))
699:
All manufactured homes must be located on an approved site where the minimum lot size shall be 7,500 square feet.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 14-6(b))
700:
Permanent connection required. All manufactured homes must be permanently connected to water, sewerage and electrical service.
Water. Water service shall be public. Connection procedures must meet the requirements of the city's building and technical codes and must be freezeproof above and below ground. The water connection must be inspected and approved by the building official and the water system must be approved by the county health department.
Sewer. Plumbing for sewage must meet the requirements of the city's building and technical codes and any applicable county health department requirements. The sewerage system must be approved by the county health department.
Electrical. Electrical service must meet requirements of the city's building and technical codes. Electrical connections must be inspected and approved by the building official prior to authorization to the servicing power company to install permanent power service.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 14-7(a))
701:
All manufactured homes must be installed on a pier system, installed with permanent skirting, secured with tie-down devices and provided with steps and landings. The installation of all required foundation requirements must be inspected and approved by the building official.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 14-7(b))
702:
Piers or load-bearing supports or devices shall be designed and constructed to evenly distribute the loads. Piers shall be securely attached to the frame of the manufactured home or shall extend at least six inches from the centerline of the frame member. Manufactured load-bearing supports or devices shall be listed or approved for the use intended, or piers shall be constructed as follows:
Piers less than 40 inches in height shall be constructed of open or closed cell, eight-inch by eight-inch by 16-inch concrete blocks (with open cells vertically placed upon the footer). Single-stacked block piers shall be installed with the 16-inch dimensions perpendicular to the main (I-beam) frame. The piers shall be covered with a two-inch by eight-inch by 16-inch pressure treated wood or concrete.
Piers between 40 and 80 inches in height and all corner piers over three blocks high shall be double blocked with blocks interlocked and capped with a four-inch by 16-inch by 16-inch solid concrete block, or equivalent.
Piers over 80 inches in height shall be constructed in accordance with this section and they shall be laid in concrete mortar and steel reinforcing bars inserted in block cells with the block cells filled with concrete.
All piers shall be placed on footings of solid concrete not less than 16 inches by 16 inches by four inches.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 14-7(b)(1))
703:
Installation of skirting shall be required. Installation shall be in accordance with the manufacturer's installation instructions. Acceptable materials may include masonry, stone or brick material for the purpose of skirting.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 14-7(b)(2))
704:
Each manufactured home shall have tie downs or other devices securing the stability of the manufactured home as per installation of manufactured homes and mobile homes rules and regulations established and published by the state safety fire commissioner and O.C.G.A. § 8-2-160 et seq.
The requirements for units 14 feet and less in width require two types of anchorage: over the top tie downs to restrict overturning and frame tie downs to restrict the unit from being pushed from its piers. The requirements for units over 14 feet in width ("doublewides") require frame tie downs only.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 14-7(b)(3))
705:
Steps and landings are required for all homes and shall be constructed to the standards set forth in the city's building and technical codes.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 14-7(b)(4))
708:
Permitted locations. Manufactured homes qualifying as single-family dwellings shall be regulated uniformly with other housing constructed on site, subject to requirements and limitations set forth in this chapter.
Compatibility standards. Compatibility standards for manufactured homes meeting the definition of a single-family dwelling are as follows: Minimum width in excess of 16 feet. Minimum square footage required by the zone in which located. Roof with a minimum 2:12 (two inches of rise for every 12 inches of run) roof pitch and a surface of wood shakes, asphalt composition, wood shingles, concrete, fiberglass or metal tiles, slate, built-up gravel materials, or other materials approved by the building official. Exterior siding materials consisting of wood, masonry, concrete, stucco, Masonite, metal or vinyl or other materials of like appearance. Attachment to a permanent foundation. Construction according to standards established either by the state minimum standard codes as amended from time to time for site-build homes or the National Manufactured Housing Construction and Safety Standards Act of 1974, 42 USC 5401 et seq. for manufactured homes or the state industrialized building regulations, O.C.G.A. § 8-2-110 et seq., for residential industrialized buildings, provided that each of these codes shall be applicable to the specific structure to which it applies. Removal of all towing devices, wheels, axles and hitches. Landing at each exterior door that is a minimum of 36 inches by 48 inches.
Comparison to housing in immediate vicinity. Manufactured homes qualifying as a single-family dwelling shall be compared to site build and other housing in the immediate general area within the same zoning or residential district or area. Approval shall be granted upon the finding that the manufactured home is substantially similar or superior in size, siding material, roof material, foundation and general aesthetic appearance to site-built or other forms of housing which may be permitted in the same general area under this chapter or existing development or proposed development in the same area.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 14-8; Ord. of 4-2-2024, § 4)
709:
Manufactured homes which do not meet the definition of a single-family dwelling shall be permitted within areas designated as manufactured home communities, subject to the requirements of this chapter. Manufactured home communities are allowed in the RMH district subject to the requirements of this chapter.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 14-9)
713:
In their interpretation and application, the provisions of this article shall be considered minimum requirements adopted for the promotion of the public health, safety, morals, convenience, order, prosperity and general welfare of the community.
(Ord. of 12-2003, §§ 4-1.2, 21-2)
714:
Sale or conveyance of subdivided land. No person, firm, partnership, joint venture, corporation, or other legal entity, or agent therefor or representative thereof, shall transfer, convey, sell, agree to sell or negotiate to sell any part of a subdivision of land by reference to or exhibition of a plat which has not been prepared, approved and recorded according to these regulations.
Submissions to building official. No subdivision shall be approved unless the developer or his agent has submitted to the building official the required fees, plats and plans as described in these regulations, has obtained approval of all plats and plans, including approval of the final plat or plan, by the city council or building official, and the approved final plat is recorded with the clerk or the superior court.
Filing and recording. No plat of a subdivision within the city shall be filed or recorded by the clerk of county superior court until the final plat shall have been prepared, submitted to, approved and recorded according to these regulations.
Acceptance by city. The city shall not accept any subdivision not designed, developed and recorded in accordance with the provisions of these regulations, nor shall it improve, maintain, grade or pave any street within such subdivision unless such street shall have met the specifications described herein.
Unauthorized conveyances. No lot, street, alley, improvement, easement, right-of-way or other property or property right of any kind shall be conveyed, by deed or otherwise, to the city, the city council or other public authority without its express acceptance of such conveyance as indicated by the signature of its authorized agent on such deed or other document of conveyance.
Utility services. The city shall not authorize the extension of water service, sewer service, or other publicly operated services of any subdivision not designed, developed and recorded in accordance with the provisions of these regulations or to extend utility services to any parcel created in violation of these regulations.
Building permits. No building permit shall be issued for the construction of any building or structure located on a lot or plat subdivided or sold in violation of the provisions of these regulations, nor shall the city have any obligation to issue certificates of occupancy or to extend utility services to any parcel created in violation of these regulations.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 21-2)
715:
All land physically unsuitable for subdivision shall not be improved. This includes:
Property affected by flooding, bad drainage, steep slopes, rock formations, or other such features which may endanger health, life or property, aggravate erosion, increase flood hazard, or necessitate excessive expenditures of public funds for supply or maintenance of services.
Property which other public agencies concerned have investigated and found in the best interest of the public not suitable for the type of platting and development proposed. Such property shall not be approved for subdivision unless adequate methods are formulated by the developer for meeting the problems created by subdivision of such property.
The mayor and city council shall not approve what it considers to be scattered or premature subdivision of land which would endanger the health, safety and general welfare of city residents or property because of lack of or adverse effect on the city's water supply, schools, drainage, adequate transportation or other public services.
The mayor and city council shall not approve a subdivision where the soil conditions have been determined not suitable for development by the city health department pursuant to local, state, and federal laws, regulations and standards.
(Ord. of 12-2003, §§ 4-7, 8-10)
716:
The name of each subdivision must have the approval of the mayor and city council. The name shall not duplicate or closely approximate the name of an existing subdivision.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 8-9)
717:
Except as hereinafter provided, no building or structure shall be erected on a lot unless such building or structure, enlargement, additions or alterations conform to the area regulations and setback requirements of the zone in which it is located.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 4-2)
718:
No lot shall be reduced, diminished and so maintained that the yards, other open space or total lot area shall be smaller than prescribed by this chapter. This section shall not apply when a portion of a lot is acquired for public use.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 4-3)
719:
No building or structure shall hereafter be erected, constructed, reconstructed or altered to:
Exceed the height limit established for the zone wherein such building or structure is located;
Exceed the number of families or occupy a smaller lot area per family; or
Reduce or diminish front yards, rear yards, side yards, or other open spaces;unless in conformity with all of the regulations herein specified for the district in which it is located.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 4-4)
720:
No part of a yard or other open space or the off-street parking or loading spaces required around any building or structure for the purpose of complying with the provisions of this chapter shall be included as a part of the yard or open space or off-street parking or loading spaces required for another building or structure.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 4-5)
721:
Only one principal building and its customary accessory buildings may hereinafter be erected on any lot.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 4-6)
722:
If a proposed subdivision includes land that is zoned for commercial or industrial purposes, the layout of the subdivision with respect to the land shall make provision as the mayor and city council may require. Site plan approval and nonresidential subdivision plat approval may proceed simultaneously at the discretion of the mayor and city council.
A nonresidential subdivision shall be subject to all the requirements of these regulations, as well as such additional standards required by the mayor and city council, and shall conform to the proposed land use standards established in the comprehensive plan.
In addition to the principles and standards in these regulations, which are appropriate to the planning of all subdivisions, the applicant shall demonstrate to the satisfaction of the mayor and city council that the street, parcel, and block pattern proposed is specifically adapted to the uses anticipated and takes into account other uses in the vicinity. The following principles and standards shall be observed: All proposed industrial parcels shall be suitable in area and dimension to the types of industrial development anticipated. Street rights-of-way and pavement shall be adequate to accommodate the type and volume of traffic anticipated to be generated thereupon. Special requirements may be imposed by the city with respect to street, curb, gutter, and sidewalk design and construction. Special requirements may be imposed by the city with respect to the installation of public utilities, including water, sewer, and storm water drainage. Every effort shall be made to protect adjacent residential areas from potential nuisance from a proposed commercial or industrial subdivision, including the provision of extra depth in parcels backing up on existing or potential residential development and provisions for a permanently landscaped buffer strip when necessary. Streets carrying nonresidential traffic, especially truck traffic, shall not normally be extended to the boundaries of adjacent existing or potential areas.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 4-8)
723:
A subdivision plat that represents four lots or less fronting on a public street shall not be subject to the requirements for improvements and design specified in this article if it meets the following conditions: The original tract for subdivision fronts for a distance of 150 feet on a public street which is identified as such on the official city road map, as adopted by the mayor and city council. The size and zoning classification of each lot resulting from the subdivision shall meet the minimum standards set forth in the city zoning regulations.
Platted lots on streets and roads which have been accepted as part of established subdivisions under the minimum standards of this article cannot be further subdivided unless such future subdivision was made part of the original approval of the plat of such subdivision or more than five years has passed since the original subdivision of the subject property.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 4-9; Ord. of 6-2-2026)
724:
The subdivision of land abutting on private roads shall be allowed only under exceptional circumstances. Prior to approval, the developer shall furnish proof to the mayor and city council that: Said roads will be maintained in perpetuity as private roads; Each owner of the lots abutting on such road owns as undivided interest in the road; or The developer has ensured by some other method acceptable to the city council that such private roads are not public, not the responsibility of the city, and will be adequately maintained.
The mayor and city council shall be provided such documents as may be required by them to ensure that the foregoing provisions have been established for the maintenance of such private roads. Such documents shall be in a form suitable for recordation in the office of the clerk of the county superior court and shall be approved by the city attorney.
As a condition to approval, the mayor and city council may require that private roads be developed in accordance with all or a portion of the standards in this article.
An appropriate permanent sign identifying such roads as private will be erected by the developer or owners at all locations where private roads intersect with public roads.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 4-10)
727:
The owner of any land lying within the area of jurisdiction of these regulations who wishes to subdivide such land shall seek plat approval by the mayor and city council according to the procedures provided in this division.
(Ord. of 12-2003, art. 5, intro.)
728:
The statutory period required for formal approval, conditional approval or disapproval of the preliminary or final plat submittal shall begin on the official submission date. The official submission date for a preliminary plat is the date of the conclusion of the plat hearing before the city council. The official submission date for a final plat is the date of the conclusion of the public meeting for consideration of the plat.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 5-1)
729:
Prior to the review, consideration and approval of a preliminary plat by the mayor and city council, the subdivider may schedule an initial meeting with the building official to discuss the proposed development. The developer may offer a simple sketch plan showing existing conditions within the site and in its vicinity and the proposed layout and development of the subdivision to the building official.
The purpose of the meeting is to assist the subdivider with questions he may have prior to extensive site planning necessary for the preparation of the preliminary plat and to enable the subdivider to become familiar with the regulations affecting the land to be subdivided.
Recommendations received from the building official concerning the proposed development or the sketch plan do not authorize the developer to begin the proposed construction or improvements.
No fee shall be charged for this informal consultation and no formal application shall be required.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 5-2)
730:
Prior to making any street improvements or installing any utilities, the prospective subdivider shall submit to the mayor and city council a preliminary plat. Approval of the preliminary plat by the mayor and city council constitutes authorization for the subdivider to develop the subdivision subject to the minimum standards for required improvements and design standards.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 5-3)
731:
After approval of the preliminary plat by the mayor and city council, the subdivider may proceed with the preparation of the final plat and other documents as may be required in connection therewith. No final plat shall be approved by the mayor and city council until either:
The required improvements listed are constructed in satisfactory manner and approved by the building official and the mayor and city council; or
In lieu of such prior construction, the mayor and city council has accepted an approved bond or security in the amount equal to the estimated cost of installation and completion of the required improvements, whereby improvements may be made and utilities installed without cost to the city in the event of default by the subdivider.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 5-4)
734:
The application for preliminary approval of a subdivision plat shall be submitted to the building official together with the appropriate fee as determined by the mayor and city council. The building official shall check the plat for conformance to these regulations and report his findings and recommendations to the zoning board. The zoning board shall then review the application for preliminary plat approval and make a recommendation to the mayor and city council who shall afford a hearing on the preliminary plat. No preliminary plat shall be approved by the mayor and city council without full compliance with the requirements of the preliminary plat.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 6-1)
735:
Upon receipt of the zoning board's recommendations, the mayor and city council shall call a public hearing for the next scheduled meeting of the mayor and city council to be held at least 30 days after the date of the application.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 6-2)
736:
Public notice of the hearing on the application for preliminary plat approval shall be given at least 15, but not more than 45, days prior to the scheduled public hearing. The building official shall file a notice of public hearing which shall be published in a newspaper of general circulation in the county setting forth the time, place, and purpose of the hearing. Such notice shall identify the property affected. The cost of such newspaper notice shall be paid by the applicant for preliminary plat approval.
Additionally, at least 15 days before the scheduled public hearing, the building official shall post in a conspicuous place on the property a sign at least two feet by three feet in size. It shall set forth the time, place and purpose of the public hearing before the mayor and city council. Acts of vandalism or natural occurrences limiting the effectiveness of notice by a sign posted on the property shall not invalidate any proceedings or action taken under this chapter.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 6-3)
737:
The mayor and city council shall approve, disapprove or approve with modification, the preliminary plat within 45 days after the date it is presented at the public hearing. The mayor and city council shall consider the recommendations of the zoning board when rendering a decision. If approved, the mayor and city council shall indicate so in writing, stating the conditions of such approval, if any, or, if disapproved, the mayor and city council shall express in writing its disapproval and its reasons therefor.
Failure of the mayor and city council to act within 45 days after the preliminary plat is presented at the public hearing shall be deemed to constitute approval, and a certificate to that effect shall be issued by the mayor and city council on demand; provided; however, that the subdivider may waive this requirement and consent in writing to the extension of such period.
Preliminary approval of the subdivision plat shall be noted on the plat and certified by the mayor and city council. Also noted shall be the date on which the mayor and city council granted preliminary approval and the date of written notification to the subdivider or subdivider's authorized agent.
Approval of a preliminary subdivision plat shall not constitute approval of the final subdivision plat. Preliminary approval shall constitute approval of the proposed widths and alignments of streets and the dimensions and shapes of lots subject to the final approval of the city health department. Application for approval of the final record plat will be considered only after the requirements for final plat approval as specified herein have been fulfilled and after all other specified conditions have been met.
Upon approval of the preliminary subdivision plat by the mayor and city council, the subdivider may proceed to comply with the other requirements of these regulations and the preparation of the final subdivision plat.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 6-4)
738:
No preliminary plat of a proposed subdivision shall be recommended for approval by the zoning board or approved by the mayor and city council unless the applicant proves by clear and convincing evidence that: Definite provision has been made for a water supply system that is sufficient in terms of quantity, dependability, and quality to provide an appropriate supply of water for the type of subdivision proposed; If a public sewage system is proposed, adequate provision has been made for such a system and, if other methods of sewage disposal are proposed, that such systems will comply with federal, state, and local laws and regulations; All proposed streets on the preliminary plat are in conformity with adopted design standards, and existing and proposed public street improvements; All areas of the proposed subdivision which may involve soil or topographical conditions presenting hazards or requiring special precautions have been identified by the subdivider and the proposed uses of these areas are compatible with such conditions; The subdivider has the financial ability to complete the proposed subdivision in accordance with all applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations; There is no other available subdivided land in the jurisdiction of the city that would be more suitable for the applicant's proposed uses of the subdivision; The proposed subdivision will not result in the scattered subdivision of land that leaves undeveloped parcels of land lacking urban services between developed parcels; The subdivider has taken every effort to mitigate the impact of the proposed subdivision on public health, safety, and welfare.
The mayor and city council are authorized to disapprove the preliminary plat even though the proposed use is consistent with the comprehensive plan.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 6-5)
739:
The mayor and city council may require that all public improvements be installed and dedicated prior to the signing of the final subdivision plat. If the mayor and city council does not require that all public improvements be installed and dedicated prior to signing of the final subdivision plat, the mayor and city council shall require that the applicant execute performance and maintenance guarantees. The mayor and city council shall require the applicant to indicate on the plat all roads and public utility improvements which shall be required to be established or extended, and any other special requirements deemed necessary by the mayor and city council in order for the subdivision plat to conform to the city comprehensive plan.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 6-6)
740:
The approval of a preliminary plat shall be effective for a period of one year from the date that the preliminary plat is approved by the mayor and city council, at the end of which time the applicant must have submitted a final subdivision plat for approval. If a subdivision plat is not submitted for final approval within the one-year period, the preliminary approval shall be null and void, and the applicant shall be required to submit a new plat for preliminary plat review subject to the then existing subdivision regulations.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 6-7)
741:
The preliminary plat shall be drawn to a scale of not less than one inch equals 100 feet and meet the minimum standards of design set forth in these regulations. The plat shall be submitted in not less than five blueline prints and shall be such as to meet the minimum requirements contained herein. The sheet size shall not exceed 18 inches by 24 inches nor be less that 8½ inches by 11 inches. It shall include the following information:
General information. Full name of proposed subdivision. Name, address, and telephone number of petitioner and architect, surveyor, engineer or designer. All names and addresses of all property owners of the site. All names and addresses of adjoining subdivisions or all deed record owners of the land adjacent to the site. Date, scale, and north arrow on map. Location or vicinity map at a scale of not less than one inch equals one mile tying the subdivision into the present road system and relating the subdivision to its surrounding area. Acreage to be subdivided. A written legal description (metes and bounds with all bearing and distances) of the acreage to be subdivided. Proper identification of the boundaries of the tract to be subdivided with all bearings and distances indicated. The boundary survey shall be to such a degree of accuracy that the error of closure is 1:7,500 or greater.
Existing conditions. Topographic map on a scale of one inch representing 100 feet or less and contour intervals of five feet or less, showing major watercourses, marshes, rock outcrops, wooded areas, and other outstanding features. In case of resubdivision, a copy of the existing plat with proposed resubdivision superimposed thereon. Location of natural features such as streams, lakes, swamps, and land subject to flood based on a 100-year flood frequency on the property to be subdivided. Exact boundary lines of the tract to be subdivided, by bearings and distances; lot lines with approximate dimensions; minimum front building setback line. Location of existing buildings on the property to be subdivided. Location and right-of-way of streets, roads, railroads and utility lines, either on or adjacent to the property to be subdivided, with statement as to whether utility lines are in easements or right-of-way and show location of poles or towers. Size and location of existing sewers, water mains, drains, culverts or other underground facilities within the street or within the right-of-way of streets or roads adjoining the tract. Grades and invert elevations of sewers shall be shown. The acreage of each drainage area affecting the proposed subdivision. All elevations shall refer to mean sea level datum where public water and/or public sewers are to be installed. Location of city limit lines. Location of any wetlands situated on the property to be subdivided.
Proposed conditions. Layout of streets, roads, alleys, public crosswalks, with widths, road names, or designations, grades and cross sections. Profile of proposed streets showing natural and finished grades with percent of grade slope. Detailed layout of all lots, including building setback lines, scaled dimensions on lots, utility easements with width and use. The layout of the water distribution system showing connections to existing or proposed water supply systems; evidence of approval of the water system plans by city engineer. The layout of the sewerage system showing connections to public sewerage systems (where required) and evidence of approval of system plans by city engineer and any other state or local agencies or officers having jurisdiction over such systems (approval of city health officer where on-site disposal is to be used or approval of state water quality control board where private sewerage is to be provided). The layout of storm and surface water drainage system and evidence of approval of system plans by city engineer and by the soil erosion and sedimentation control regulations of the city. Designation of all land (if any) to be reserved or dedicated for public use. Designation of proposed use of all lots to be used for other than single-family residential (if any). Proposed major contour changes to areas where substantial cut and/or fill is to be done. A timing schedule indicating the anticipated starting and completion dates of the development sequence and the time of exposure of each area prior to the completion of effective erosion and sediment control measures. Any adjoining areas to be developed at a later date by the subdivider as an extension of or addition to the proposed subdivision as part of a continuing or long-range development plan. Total number of lots, total acreage, total length and width of new streets.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 6-8.3)
742:
A certificate of approval of the preliminary plat, in the form approved by the building official, shall be inscribed on the plat indicating the building official's approval thereof.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 6-9)
745:
Dedications. The application for final plat approval shall be accompanied by all formal irrevocable offers of dedication to the public of all streets, local government uses, utilities, parks, and easements, in a form approved by the city attorney; and the subdivision plat shall be marked with a notation indicating the formal offers of dedication as follows:"The owner, or his representative, hereby irrevocably offers for dedication to the local government all the streets, local government uses, easements, parks, and required utilities shown on the subdivision plat and construction plans in accordance with an irrevocable offer of dedication dated and recorded with the Lincoln County Clerk of Superior Court."
Documents for recording. The applicant shall deliver a full covenant and warranty deed to all dedicated lands and improvements in proper form for recording, together with a title policy for the local government in the sum not less than $10,000.00, which sum shall be determined by the city attorney before signing of the final subdivision plat.
Review by building official. The application for final approval of the subdivision plat shall be submitted to the building official, who shall examine the final plat to determine if: It meets all requirements of these regulations; Conforms to the approved preliminary plat; Has approval of the health department; Design of the roads has been approved by the city engineer; and Streets and easements have been dedicated or qualify for dedication. The final subdivision plat shall include an original and two duplicate copies prepared in accordance with the provisions of this article.
Review by zoning board. The building official shall then submit the final plat application to the zoning board, which shall review the application for final subdivision plat approval. The zoning board shall then report its recommendations to the mayor and city council, which shall afford a final subdivision plat determination.
(Ord. of 12-2003, § 7-1)
